units.source_text: 不，不對，我仍屬於那種不帶著失敗的丑角式苦笑，就無法跟他者打招呼的人。

en.t: No, that is not right; I am still the sort of person who cannot greet anyone without wearing the bitter clownish smile of defeat.

units.source_text: 總之，即便是驚慌忘我結結巴巴，也能與人打招呼了。

en.t: In any case, even if I was flustered, beside myself, and stammering, I had become able to greet people.

units.source_text: 這種能打招呼的「伎倆」，難道是以前為地下運動四處奔波而磨鍊出來的？

en.t: Was this little trick of being able to greet people something I had honed long ago while running around for the underground movement?
Or was it because of women?
Or perhaps because of heavy drinking?

units.source_text: 但主要還得歸功於手頭的拮据。

en.t: But above all, I owed it to being short of money.

units.source_text: 不論身在何處，我都會感到恐懼與不安，

en.t: No matter where I was, I felt fear and unease,

units.source_text: 反而如果在大型咖啡館，在很多醉漢、女服務員、男服務員的擁來擠去裡，自己不斷被追逐的心靈不是也能獲得平靜嗎？

en.t: and yet, if I were in a large cafe, jostled and swallowed up among many drunks, waitresses, and waiters, might not my constantly pursued heart find some calm?
